output.best_reason: Version C best balances the four criteria. Félix's voice is distinct and consistent: he is defensive, self-aware, and a little cruel about his uncle ("Not enough, I thought"). The period texture comes from the characters' concerns, such as the repeater meant to strike the first minute of the new century, rather than from costume-drama phrasing. Tension builds because Félix anticipates how his position will look ("I can hear it already"). The timeline arrives inside his arguments and corrections instead of as a recited list. Version E has the sharpest individual lines, but its interviewer leans on stock questions ("Were you frightened?", "How did that make you feel?"). Version D is restrained and well judged but less distinctive. Version A is solid but more conventional in its rhythm. Version B ends on a literal recap of the facts ("The thump. The repeater. The stairs, twice."), which exposes the recited-list problem the brief warns against.
